missionPremise: Operator ruling 2026-08-31 (_decisions/2026-08-31_next_action_rail_activation_engine.md), four parts: the Settings right rail becomes ACTION not information; capability-first, so an action names what you get and never a price or a plan; a MOUNTABLE COMPONENT not a Settings feature, because Settings is low traffic and a funnel engine that only fires there moves almost nothing; and instrumented from the first commit, because the locked GTM plan names activation instrumentation as the blocker for affiliate optimisation. The acceptance test is that the ladder must be able to return NOTHING: a next-action surface that always finds something to sell is an ad slot, and this panel already declares that nothing in it is a control that does nothing.

LESSON: A calendar word ('today', 'tomorrow') derived from a UTC instant is an unearned claim when the module does not know the viewer's timezone. Say a DURATION and round DOWN - understating is the safe direction for an expiry warning. Caught by the test on its first run.

A parse that drops unrecognised rows returns [] on a whole-contract mismatch, and [] is then indistinguishable from an honest empty. Rule: rows arrived and NONE could be shaped is UNREADABLE, not empty. A partial drop may still keep the good rows.

When two halves of a contract are authored in different repos, a parity test that retypes the path is a THIRD copy - a matching typo on both sides passes. Import the client's own path constant so the test compares the two independently authored halves.

perl/sed substitutions whose patterns span a newline SILENTLY NO-OP on CRLF files in a Windows checkout, and a violation harness then reports the check as vacuous when no mutation was ever made. Any mutation harness must assert the pattern was FOUND before scoring the result. In this repo new files are LF and existing tracked files are CRLF, so the same script can work on one and no-op on the next.

A violation battery must record WHICH gate fails. One of thirteen here fails the TYPE CHECKER and not vitest, because Date.parse(null) is NaN and a downstream guard absorbs it. That is a stronger mechanism, but reporting it as 'a test catches it' would be false.

A next-action ladder needs a host-side runnable set. The ladder is host-agnostic by design, so the host must be able to say 'I have no working control for this step' and render nothing, fail-closed. Without it the rail ships a dead button the moment the server half lands.
Where a clock and the data it interprets come from the same response, put the clock INSIDE the read arm and delete the caller-supplied one. Two derivations of 'now' are free to disagree; one cannot.
DEAD-END: Adding fetchAccountEntitlement() to entitlementClient.ts to feed the plan rungs. Measured before building: it would supply tier and subscriptionTier but NOT freeMessagesLeft (per-property, inside the response's property block), NOT billingInterval (not on the wire at all) and NOT seats (roster route 404s). Zero additional rungs would fire. Rejected as scope creep with no payoff.

Routing unlock_expiring through onUpgrade from Settings. ExplorerMap passes parcelNodeId={activeParcelNodeId} to PricingModal, so the checkout would be scoped to whatever parcel the MAP has selected - possibly a different property from the one lapsing. Worse than not offering the step.
Keeping a `label` field on AccountUnlock. The server's shape has no such field; a nullable label that is always null is a slot inviting someone to fill it from parcelNodeId.
